hints.content:
We are trying to find a **unit rate**, specifically the earnings, in dollars, per $1$ hour of work.

$\dfrac{\blueE{\text{total earnings}}}{\maroonD{\text{hours}}} = \purpleD{\text{earnings per hour}}$

We can compare from the largest to the smallest place value.

###Finding the unit rates

We divide based on the unit rate we want.

Employee| $\blueE{\text{Total earnings}} $ || $\maroonD{\text{Hours of}}$ $\maroonD{\text{work}}$||$\purpleD{\text{Earnings}}$ $\purpleE{\text{per hour}}$ 
- | :-: | :-:| :-:|:-:|:-:
$A$ |$180$|$\div$ | $15$|$=$|$12$
$B$|$210$ |$\div$ |$20$ | $=$|$10.5$
$C$ |$455$ |$\div$ | $35$|$=$| $13 $

###Comparing the unit rates

Employee | Tens | Ones | $.$ | Tenths
- | :-: | :-:| :-:|:-:|:-:
 $A$ | $1$ | $2$ | $.$ | $0$
$B$| $1$ | $0$ | $.$ | $5$
$C$ | $1$ | $\redE{3}$ | $.$ | $0$

The employees all earn $1$ ten of dollars per hour, but employee C earns the most ones of dollars per hour.

###Conclusion

Employee $C$ has the highest earnings per hour.

question.content:
Three employees each clocked a different number of hours worked this week.

Employee | Total earnings (in dollars) | Hours of work
- | :-: | :-:
$A$ | $180$ | $15$
$B$ | $210$ | $20$
$C$ | $455$ | $35$

**Which employee has the highest earnings per hour?**
